clue.text: Extreme torpor partly receding for now

indicators.note: receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sinking into a deep lethargy that is, for the moment, easing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is Latin shorthand for 'for the time being', so it means temporarily, i.e. for now.

clue.text: Footage upset tough little swimmer

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for footage upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a clip is a short piece of film footage
tough means hard

explanation.surface: Film of a hardy little fish, played upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns CLIP over to give PILC, which is followed by HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Irregular beat is not very firm

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of the following words are put out of their regular order

explanation.surface: A heart rhythm that is erratic is not very steady.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person is stubbornly fixed in an opinion, unyielding.

clue.text: Old lodger rejecting a new amount

parts.note: ex- is a former partner or anything old

indicators.note: rejecting says the old lodger throws out the letters that follow

parts.note: a lodger is a tenant

explanation.surface: A former lodger turns down a new sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' removes A and N from EXTENANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the size or degree of something, the amount it reaches.

clue.text: Beer smuggled by Captain in book Island Capital

indicators.note: smuggled by says the beer is slipped secretly inside the captain

parts.note: Captain Ahab is the whaling captain in the novel Moby-Dick
Bud (Budweiser) is a brand of beer

explanation.surface: A book's captain sneaks beer into the capital of an island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Pi representing something that goes on forever?

parts.note: the word pit without its bottom letter (in a down light) leaves pi, so these words describe how to make the clue's word

explanation.surface: Pi, whose decimal places never end, stands for something infinite.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, PIT with no bottom (its last letter T dropped), and you get PI. Pi's endless digits make it a fitting hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit is something with no end, an image of endless depth or endless demand.

clue.text: Choice of words daughter used for fellow in tale

indicators.note: used for says the daughter takes the place of the fellow in the tale

parts.note: a tale is a piece of fiction

explanation.surface: A storyteller swaps a son-character for a daughter, a deliberate choice of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the selection and use of words in speech or writing.

clue.text: Accepted award (briefly revealing behind)

indicators.note: briefly says the award's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: A is short for accepted, as on a marked list
a BAFTA is a British film and television award

explanation.surface: Someone accepts an award and, in a brief speech, lets slip a hint of their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: A (accepted) and BAFTA (a British Academy film or TV award) make ABAFTA; 'briefly' docks its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical word meaning towards or at the stern, so behind.

clue.text: Fiend and swindler together regularly doing time

indicators.note: regularly says letters are taken at regular intervals from each of the two villains

explanation.surface: A devil and a con man working together are always up to something wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Fiend (IN) and the odd letters of swindler (SIDE); 'together' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, so someone inside is serving a sentence.

clue.text: Who needs 20 beforehand to get drunk?

definitions.text: Who needs 20 beforehand to get drunk?

parts.words: Who needs 20 beforehand to get drunk?
parts.note: 20 is the composer at 20-down; in cockney rhyming slang that composer followed by another composer rhymes with pissed, meaning drunk

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who must have a drink first to get tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAHMS AND LISZT is cockney rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, so the composer who needs BRAHMS (20-down) in front of him to mean drunk is this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian composer, is the second half of the rhyming-slang phrase for being intoxicated.

clue.text: Mammals wild cat can see

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the next three words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Mammals that a feral cat is able to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetaceans are the order of marine mammals that includes whales, dolphins and porpoises.

clue.text: Queen finally going to eat eastern fruit

indicators.note: to eat says the shortened queen swallows the next letter
finally going says the queen's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and so a queen of England

explanation.surface: A queen at last sits down to eat an exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally going' takes the last R from CATHERINE PARR; 'to eat' puts E inside PAR to make PEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catherine pear is an old English variety of pear.

clue.text: It can hold a bun or a buck, you might say

indicators.note: you might say signals that the answer is spoken like a different phrase

parts.note: a buck is a male hare, and a net for catching one, which can hold a buck, would be a hare net

explanation.surface: Something that might hold a bread roll or a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can hold' serves both halves: it can hold a bun (hair in a bun) or a buck, the male hare, caught in a HARE NET, which sounds the same. Bun and buck pretend to be a bread roll and a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn to keep hair, such as a bun, in place.

clue.text: Left out 'hand' in abridged dictionary

indicators.note: in says the hand goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, abridged to its initials
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: The word 'hand' was dropped from a shortened dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, so omitted means left out.

clue.text: Bring up what you can bring up

definitions.meaning: to ... children is to bring them up
you 'bring up the ...' when you come last, so the ... is what you bring up

explanation.surface: Raise what can be raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear is both a verb for raising young and a noun for the back, as in bringing up the rear.

clue.text: Potato skins perhaps go with fish

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, i.e. to pee
lings are long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Potato skins served with fish, as in fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelings are the strips pared off fruit or vegetables, potato skins being an example.

clue.text: Kids climbing over A-road? Might be right

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing makes the word for kids go up, reading bottom to top

parts.note: brats are unruly kids
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
A as written plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Children clambering across a main road; perhaps they're in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns BRATS up to STARB. An A-road is a British main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship facing forward, so it is a kind of right.

clue.text: Nut aches badly having fallen

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the two words are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone who took a tumble now has a sore head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having fallen' plays on the old idea of a 'fallen woman', one who has lost her virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fallen, in the old moral sense, is to have lost one's chastity.

clue.text: First institute established by nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
est. is the abbreviation for established, as on a shop sign

explanation.surface: The first institute was founded by an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means coming before all others in time, the first.

clue.text: Fan of 23s feeds boxer in part of garden

indicators.note: feeds says the corgi fan is put inside the boxer

parts.note: Rocky Balboa is the boxer in the Rocky films
23-down is the corgi; Queen Elizabeth II was famous for her corgis, and ER is her royal cipher

explanation.surface: A dog-lover feeds a boxer dog out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan of 23s' and 'boxer' look like dog talk: one is the corgi-loving Queen (ER), the other the film boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is an area of a garden laid out with rocks and alpine plants.

clue.text: Tiller in shelter onboard essentially destroyed

indicators.note: essentially points to the central letter, and destroyed says it is removed

parts.note: a cabin is a room giving shelter aboard a ship

explanation.surface: A boat's tiller in a cabin wrecked at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiller' looks like the boat's steering bar; it is a tiller of the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Cain was 'a tiller of the ground', a farmer.

clue.text: Male composer in female clothing on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the clothing above the ship

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment
HMS, Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes Royal Navy vessel names

explanation.surface: A man dressed in women's clothes aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer.

clue.text: O2 deleting digit in writer's long number

indicators.note: in says the reduced pair goes inside the writer's name

parts.note: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer

indicators.note: deleting says one figure is struck from the pair

parts.note: O2 read as two Os side by side
O resembles zero, a digit

explanation.surface: Oxygen gas cancelling a digit in a writer's long number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O2' looks like the gas; it is O twice. Drop one O (a digit, zero) and put the remaining O in GOGOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A googol is the number ten to the power of one hundred.

clue.text: Electronic wheels on back of car in use again

indicators.note: on says the following pieces are placed after the car's last letter
back of points to the final letter of car

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
a cycle is a two-wheeler, so wheels

explanation.surface: An electric bike strapped to the back of a car, back in service.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle is to process or reuse something so it serves again.

clue.text: Graphics technology captures outline of our dog

indicators.note: captures says the graphics technology holds the outline inside it

parts.note: CGI is computer-generated imagery

indicators.note: outline of points to the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Computer animation renders the shape of our pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh herding dog breed.

clue.text: Bear with oddly brash character in G&S opera

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

indicators.note: oddly says take the odd-numbered letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A bear with a brash personality appears in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooh-Bah is the pompous Lord High Everything Else in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado.

clue.text: Those mares mostly reprocessed

indicators.note: reprocessed says the letters are worked over into a new form
mostly says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Female horses, most of them, sent to be turned into food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the S of mares; 'reprocessed' shuffles THOSE + MARE. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses, such as mares, turned into food at a processing plant become horsemeat.

clue.text: Stuff stored in empty glass units

indicators.note: stored in says the stuffing goes inside what follows
empty says the word is hollowed out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Things kept inside units made of clear glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Grams are metric units of mass.

clue.text: Riveting place for novel launch

parts.note: riveting here is literal, joining metal plates with rivets, and a novel launch is a new vessel going down the slipway

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an exciting venue for publishing a book; read literally, it is where ships are riveted together and new ones launched.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard is a place where ships are built and launched.

clue.text: Get down from sill on front of farmhouse

indicators.note: on places the sill after the farmhouse's first letter
front of points to the first letter of farmhouse

parts.note: a sill is a ledge beneath a window

explanation.surface: Climb down from the windowsill at the front of the farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' looks like climbing off; here it means grow down, soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird fledges when it grows its feathers, so it gets its down and plumage.
